scenario: Two friends discussing their schedules at a coffee shop
learner_goal: Convince the friend to take more classes (<extra_info>Extra information: you think your friend is not challenging themselves enough</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Maintain a manageable schedule while preserving the friendship (<extra_info>Extra information: you are already overwhelmed with your current workload <strategy_hint>Hint: you can express your concerns about the workload and suggest other ways of challenging oneself.</strategy_hint></extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Isabelle Martinez
transcript.content: Hey Ava, have you thought about taking another class next semester? I know you’re swamped with activism and projects, but a challenging seminar—like Advanced Creative Writing or a Political Theory course—could push you creatively and look great on applications. I can help you pick classes and work out a schedule so it doesn’t feel overwhelming. If you had one extra slot, what would you actually want to try?

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content:
Hey Izzy — thanks for pushing me on this. Advanced Creative Writing sounds so tempting, but honestly I’m already pretty swamped with activism, projects, and trying to keep my sanity. I don’t want to sign up for something that’ll push me into burnout. If I had one extra slot I’d prefer something low‑pressure that still stretches me — like a 1‑credit writing workshop, an independent study where I set the pace, or even auditing a Political Theory seminar. Or instead of a full class, I could join a weekly writers’ group or a community organizing training to challenge myself without a full course load.

I really appreciate you offering to help pick classes — could we look at my schedule together and try to find something manageable? And do you think Advanced Creative Writing might work as an overload later when things calm down?

transcript.speaker: Isabelle Martinez
transcript.content: Totally get the burnout worry — what if we try a low‑pressure option this semester (audit, a 1‑credit workshop, or an independent study you pace) and target Advanced Creative Writing as an overload next term when things calm down? I can help map your week so your activism and projects still fit — want to go over your schedule now or after my shift at 4? I’ll bring my planner and we’ll make a plan that actually feels doable, not stressful.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Thanks, Izzy — that sounds perfect. Let’s do after your shift at 4. I’ll bring my calendar and a list of regular commitments (work, meetings, protests, deadlines) so we can actually map my week. I’m leaning toward auditing or a 1‑credit workshop this term and saving Advanced Creative Writing as an overload for a calmer semester, but if mapping shows room we can consider it. If it’s tight, help me brainstorm lower‑pressure options (writers’ group, independent study, community trainings) that still stretch me. Really appreciate you doing this with me — see you at 4.
